purpose: Estradiol cypionate is used to treat symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. It is also used in hormone therapy for transgender women and to treat certain conditions caused by low estrogen levels in the body. In some cases, it may be used to help with conditions related to ovarian failure.
how_it_works: This medication is a form of estrogen, which is a natural hormone your body normally makes. When your estrogen levels are low, this injection helps replace or boost those levels. It works by attaching to estrogen receptors in your body, helping your tissues and organs function more like they would with normal estrogen levels.
common_side_effects: Nausea, breast tenderness or swelling, headaches, mood changes, bloating, spotting or changes in your menstrual period, and redness or soreness at the injection site are common side effects. Weight changes and decreased sex drive can also occur.
warnings: This medication carries a risk of serious blood clots, stroke, and heart attack, especially if you smoke or are over 35. It may increase the risk of certain cancers, including breast and uterine cancer with long-term use. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, liver problems, or certain cancers. Do not use if you are pregnant.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection into the muscle, usually by a healthcare provider. For menopause symptoms, a common dose is 1 to 5 mg injected every 3 to 4 weeks. For gender-affirming hormone therapy, doses and schedules vary and are set individually by your doctor. Never adjust your dose without talking to your healthcare provider.
